In detail

A district with a well-known split reputation, and the evidence itself is mixed. The City of Kraków's own official resident-safety survey (end of 2022, published January 2023) found Nowa Huta residents reported the highest concern citywide about specific "dangerous spots" in their district (10.3%, the worst figure in the survey) — a current, official signal. Yet the same-year police breakdown grouped Nowa Huta with Czyżyny as one of the two safer pairings citywide on raw theft/sexual-offence counts, and the 2020 Otodom survey rated it a middling 3.64/5, explicitly noting it had ranked as the single safest district as recently as 2017 before declining. Historically associated with 1990s-2000s football-hooligan ("kibole") culture tied to its heavy-industry, communist-era planned-town origins, but no specific dated 2025-2026 incident matching that old reputation was found in this research — the most current, official signal (the "dangerous spots" concern share) is the one given most weight here. Sources checked: City of Kraków official resident-safety survey, krakow.pl (published January 2023); Portal Samorządowy (2022 police district data); Otodom District Ranking 2020.
